svg.title: Density altitude on a hot day at a high aerodrome

desc.style: color: rgb(34, 48, 63); fill: rgb(0, 0, 0); fill-opacity: 1; fill-rule: nonzero; stroke: none; stroke-width: 1px; stroke-opacity: 1; stroke-dasharray: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-linejoin: miter; opacity: 1; font-size: 17px; font-family: Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; text-anchor: start; dominant-baseline: auto; letter-spacing: normal; visibility: visible; paint-order: normal; marker: none;

svg.desc: An aerodrome sits at 5,500 feet pressure altitude. On a standard day the aircraft performs as though at 5,500 feet. At 35 degrees Celsius — 31 degrees warmer than standard — the air is as thin as it would be at 9,220 feet, so the aircraft performs as though nearly 4,000 feet higher, with a longer takeoff run and a poorer climb.
